LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 7.3.1 TENSE: FUTURE TIME USING WILL/SHALL

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: Future Time using will/shall
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: Future Time using will/shall, part of Strand 7 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: which feature will and shall. 1. Which words do we use to show future time? 2. How do you tell that something will happen in the future?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

1. pick sentences

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. pick sentences

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: Future Time using will/shall together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner expresses future plans using will and shall in pairs.

• Self-efficacy is developed as the learner acquires the skill of making sentences about activities they plan do in

future.

Values:
Social justice is developed as the learner shows democracy when they engage in role play activities to plan or wish for

what to do in future.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Effective Communication is realised as the learner practises basic sentence structures that express the future that they

will use in their daily communication.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner uses the concept of future time in other language areas such as Kiswahili.
